text:
alex: Heads-up — ran into an authn/authz edge case with the svc->project token handoff. Repro attached below, but short version: infra-broker minted a token scoped to project-A, sentinel proxy forwarded it when caller requested project-B, and downstream accepted it. Not good.

tara: Ugh. can you paste the minimal repro or curl?

alex: sure — here's the minimal flow we used:
```
# service calls sentinel proxy to access project-B resource
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token-from-broker>" \n  -H "X-Request-Project: project-B" \n  https://sentinel.internal/api/projects/project-B/resources

# token claims: {"sub":"svc:ingest", "project":"project-A", "aud": "redwood-svc"}
```

javier: wait — sentinel proxy should validate token.project == requested project. it used to. did we relax that check for performance?

emily: we relaxed strict project checking for service tokens because some infra flows relied on org-level delegation. sentinel currently validates signature + org aud and then allows proxying if caller is in the same org. project claim is optional for services.

alex: that yields a privilege escalation: svc with access to project-A can ask proxy to reach project-B and succeed if proxy doesn't enforce project equality.

tara: options?

alex: thinking three options: 
1) revert — require token.project == requested project for all tokens (strict but may break some infra flows).
2) broker: mint per-project scoped tokens on demand (broker enforces scope; safer but increases broker load and key distribution complexity).
3) proxy transformation: sentinel mints ephemeral project-scoped token on behalf of caller after validating org-level claim + attestation (keeps caller flow but centralizes enforcement).

javier: pros/cons quick: 1) simplest to reason about, impacts backward compat. 2) explicit least-privilege, good audit trail, needs broker change and caching. 3) keeps proxy as policy enforcement plane, avoids storing long-lived project tokens, but sentinel needs signing ability or a broker call.

emily: also consider hybrid: require project claim for user tokens but allow org-level service tokens only if broker issued an org-delegation flag. that way infra flows can opt-in.

tara: any compliance constraints? cross-project reads are sensitive for several customers — internal policy leans toward explicit project scoping unless a controlled delegation exists.

alex: proposed immediate mitigation: re-enable project equality check as a runtime feature flag in sentinel (default on for prod), and add a compatibility mode for specific infra service principals. implement short-term while we design broker/proxy transformation.

javier: I can add the runtime check + flag. will also add telemetry to count mismatches.

emily: I'll spec the broker-side change and sketch the ephemeral-token flow. will open RFC PR with diagrams.

tara: i'll add tests and an e2e that simulates broker, sentinel, and downstream acceptance.

sec-bot: Alert: flagged token-mismatch pattern increased by 3x in the last 24h (detected by anomaly rule).

alex: thanks — action items: javier adds flag + telemetry (ETA 2d), emily opens RFC (ETA 3d), tara writes e2e (ETA 4d). we'll roll the flag to staging then prod canary. tagging @javier @emily @tara for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

javier: ack, starting branch now.

emily: will post RFC link when ready.

tara: adding test matrix to repo and will ping once CI green.

alex: leaving note for oncall: if canary shows >1% auth failures for infra svc flows, auto rollback the flag.

emily: one more Q — do we need a migration plan for long-lived tokens that lack project claim? propose a short TTL rotation with broker forcing new tokens to include project claim or delegation flag. I'll include in RFC.

alex: yep include that. good catch.

(end)
